Rhamnaceae.key_door: nectar disc/hypanthium + stamens opposite petals; split capsule vs drupe

Moraceae.key_door: woody + milky latex + tiny unisexual inflorescences + multiple fruit

Urticaceae.key_door: tiny flowers + inflexed/explosive stamens + one-ovuled achene; stinging hairs optional

anchor_families.Rosaceae: 5-part woody-flower comparison; stamens usually alternate with petals and often numerous

lineage_lesson: Rosales is better learned by reproductive architecture than by overall gestalt. Rhamnaceae uses a disc flower with antipetalous stamens, Moraceae compresses many tiny flowers into multiple fruits, and Urticaceae reduces flowers to a one-ovule achene system with spring-loaded stamens.
taxonomy_notes: Source-pool Ziziphus obtusifolia is a synonym concept of current Condaliopsis obtusifolia under Kew; preserve the source name but do not teach it as a second accepted taxon.
Morus alba remains an introduced comparison rather than a native anchor.
Boehmeria and Parietaria demonstrate that stinging hairs are not a Urticaceae family requirement.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Preserve source-name provenance while teaching current accepted concepts.
Do not duplicate Rosaceae, Ulmaceae or Cannabaceae family modules; use them only as comparison anchors.
